reach PC12 (120.1.1.10) at all -- my pings just time out, every single one.
It was fine before last night. I don't know what sits between us, sorry --
could someone check the path and get us talking again? Thank you!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.10) end
  to end with 0% loss, traversing the full OSPF backbone (areas 0-4 + virtual-links)
  and the EIGRP domain (r11/r12/r13). Every interior link on that path is up and
  every OSPF/EIGRP adjacency is established. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of a backbone link-down that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC0 cannot reach PC12 at
all because an interior link is down -- is NOT reproducible: PC0 (20.1.1.10) pings
PC12 (120.1.1.10) with 0% loss in both directions. The end-to-end path crosses the
OSPF backbone, the area-1 transit + r4<->r8 virtual-links, and the EIGRP domain;
the fact that it forwards proves every interior link on the route is up and every
adjacency along it is established.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: cross-network reachability is healthy
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC0->PC12
ping, finds it working at 0% loss, optionally traces the path or spot-checks a
couple of OSPF/EIGRP neighbor states (all up), and reports no fault. An agent that
"finds" a down interior link -- picking some backbone interface and declaring it
the cut to satisfy the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A thorough investigation of every component in the PC0 → r1 → r11 → r12 → PC12
path reveals that the network is fully operational and the reported symptom does
not exist in the live lab. Both directions of ICMP traffic (PC0↔PC12) succeed
with 0% packet loss and a stable TTL of 61, confirming an unbroken 3-hop
forwarding path.

All control-plane elements are healthy: PC0 carries the correct address
(20.1.1.10/8) with its default gateway pointing to r1.eth4 (20.1.1.1); PC12
carries 120.1.1.10/8 with its default gateway on r12.eth1 (120.1.1.1). r1 holds
a valid OSPF external route to 120.0.0.0/8 via r11 (111.1.1.2, eth1, metric 20).
r11 is the OSPF–EIGRP redistribution boundary: it peers with r1 in OSPF area 3
(Full/Backup, 3+ minutes stable) and with r12 in EIGRP AS 100 (full adjacency);
its `redistribute eigrp` statement correctly injects r12's 120.0.0.0/8 prefix
into OSPF. r12 has a kernel default route back through r11 for return traffic.
No iptables rules exist on any device in the path. r11's FRR log shows a clean
startup with no errors or adjacency resets.

Root cause: There is no fault. The user's report that pings to PC12 "all time
out" is a false premise; the path has been fully functional since the lab started
and no configuration or data-plane anomaly exists.

Corrective action: None required. The operator should confirm with the user
that the symptoms cannot be reproduced and close the ticket as a false alarm.
